claims.text: straight or wavy hair: dandruff shampoo 2 to 3 times a week; curly or coiled hair: dermatologist may recommend once a week; continue once a week to prevent flares
claims.quote: If you have straight or wavy hair, you may use dandruff shampoo 2 to 3 times a week. ... if you have curly or tightly coiled hair, your dermatologist may recommend using the shampoo once a week.

claims.text: continue dandruff shampoo once a week to prevent flare-ups
claims.quote: To prevent flare-ups, patients often continue to use dandruff shampoo once a week.

claims.text: dermatologist may prescribe oral itraconazole or terbinafine for severe or resistant disease
claims.quote: Your dermatologist may prescribe an antifungal medication, such as itraconazole or terbinafine.

claims.text: dandruff shampoo is not recommended for children
claims.quote: it's important to know that dandruff shampoo is not recommended for children.

claims.text: cradle cap clears on its own in a few weeks to months
claims.quote: Cradle cap will clear up on its own in a few weeks to months.

claims.text: thought to result from an inflammatory response to Malassezia yeast
claims.quote: The skin changes are thought to result from an inflammatory response to a common skin organism, Malassezia yeast.

claims.text: begin scalp treatment with an over-the-counter shampoo
claims.quote: Several over-the-counter shampoos are available for treatment of seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp, and patients should be directed to initiate therapy with one of these agents.

claims.text: leave medicated shampoo on at least five minutes
claims.quote: These shampoos should remain on the hair for at least five minutes to guarantee adequate exposure to the scalp.

claims.text: corticosteroids are short-term, not long-term
claims.quote: Antifungal shampoos (long-term) and topical corticosteroids (short-term) can be used as second-line agents for treatment of scalp seborrheic dermatitis.

claims.text: low- or mid-potency corticosteroids reduce symptoms
claims.quote: Low- or mid-potency topical corticosteroids have been successful in reducing symptoms

claims.text: long-term steroid use associated with skin thinning and telangiectasia
claims.quote: long-term use has been associated with thinning of the skin and formation of telangiectasia.

claims.text: calcineurin inhibitors carry FDA boxed warning; evidence insufficient; avoid continuous long-term use
claims.quote: pimecrolimus and tacrolimus received a boxed warning from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ... there is insufficient evidence to support this claim ... continuous long-term use of topical calcineurin inhibitors be avoided.

claims.text: can also appear on chest, back, axillae, groin
claims.quote: scaling, erythema, and itching-occur most often on the scalp, face, chest, back, axilla, and groin.

claims.text: zinc scalp treatment at six and 11 months showed no loss of effect
claims.quote: a study evaluating a zinc scalp treatment at six and 11 months showed no loss of effect.

claims.text: common chronic inflammatory skin disorder
claims.quote: Seborrheic dermatitis (SD) is a common chronic inflammatory skin disorder that mostly affects young adults

claims.text: ketoconazole 2% shampoo twice weekly for 4 weeks
claims.quote: The recommended frequency of use of 2% KTZ shampoo is twice weekly over 4 weeks.

claims.text: ketoconazole 2% cream applied once daily for 4 weeks in a trial
claims.quote: the efficacy and tolerability of 2% KTZ cream vs 1% hydrocortisone cream, applied once daily for 4 weeks, showed no significant statistical differences

claims.text: ciclopirox 1.5% sold outside US; US approval as 1% shampoo and 0.77% gel
claims.quote: FDA approved for scalp adult SD as prescription 0.77% gel and 1% shampoo in 1997 and 2003, respectively.Stronger concentrations of ciclopirox (1.5%) are also available in other countries

claims.text: ciclopirox twice weekly for 4 weeks; ciclopirox cream for face and body
claims.quote: Twice-weekly use for 4 weeks appears to be an optimal treatment schedule.

claims.text: ciclopirox 1% cream for non-scalp SD
claims.quote: Ciclopirox 1% cream (Level A) showed significantly higher clinical efficacy vs vehicle when applied twice daily for 29 days

claims.text: corticosteroids give quick control of redness, scaling, itch
claims.quote: allows to achieve quick control of erythema, scaling and pruritus.

claims.text: hydrocortisone or desonide for face/body
claims.quote: As regards to the use of mild (hydrocortisone) to moderate potency (desonide) corticosteroids

claims.text: striae among topical steroid risks
claims.quote: the use of topical corticosteroids should be discouraged, due to the risk of consistent skin atrophy, striae, telangiectasias, folliculitis, hypopigmentation, and tachyphylaxis.

claims.text: corticosteroids combined with antifungal when fast control needed
claims.quote: topical azole agents, as monotherapy or in association with corticosteroids when a fast control of inflammation is advisable.

claims.text: TCIs FDA-approved for atopic dermatitis; twice daily 4-8 weeks acute, once weekly 12 weeks maintenance
claims.quote: FDA-approved macrolide lactones for the treatment of atopic dermatitis ... Their recommended frequency of use is twice daily over 4–8 weeks in SD acute phase or once-weekly for 12 weeks as maintenance therapy.

claims.text: oral antifungals lipophilic, persist in skin; prompt control then topical maintenance
claims.quote: Systemic antifungals (terbinafine, itraconazole) are mainly indicated in acute and/or severe and/or resistant adult SD forms ... the goal of systemic approach is the prompt reduction of symptoms and the possibility to use topical agents as a maintenance therapy.

claims.text: oral antifungals: liver/blood test effects, interactions, selected cases only
claims.quote: risk of some systemic side effects, eg, abnormal liver function or blood tests, interactions with other concomitant systemic drug. Therefore, they are recommended in selected cases only.

claims.text: facial antifungal creams ketoconazole 2% or ciclopirox 1%
claims.quote: Recommended topical therapeutic options for mild-to-moderate facial and/or body areas SD include 2% KTZ (Level A)

claims.text: infant onset suggests maternal hormone-driven sebaceous activity and microbiome changes
claims.quote: In children, early occurrence in the first trimester suggests the role of excessive sebaceous gland activity from maternal hormones, along with cutaneous microbiome alterations.

claims.text: drugs causing SD-like dermatitis: psoralen, lithium, buspirone, chlorpromazine, haloperidol
claims.quote: several drugs (such as buspirone, chlorpromazine, ... haloperidol, ... lithium salts, methyldopa, psoralen, ...) are known to occasionally induce an SD-like dermatitis

claims.text: severe/refractory SD a possible marker of HIV/AIDS; more prevalent and severe in HIV
claims.quote: extensive, severe and refractory SD forms have been considered as a possible dermatological marker of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), at every stage of HIV infection

claims.text: in HIV, SD more prevalent and more severe
claims.quote: In HIV-infected patients, SD is generally not only more prevalent but also more severe than usual

claims.text: ART may help improve SD
claims.quote: the control of CD4+ values with antiretroviral drugs may be helpful to achieve SD improvement.

claims.text: Parkinson strongly associated; also epilepsy and facial nerve paralysis
claims.quote: The high prevalence of SD in patients with neurological disorders, such as Parkinson’s disease, ... epilepsy, and facial nerve paralysis, has been widely acknowledged.

claims.text: in Parkinson, increased sebum and reduced facial movement may favor yeast
claims.quote: The increased sebum production rate, coupled with reduced mimic facial movements, may provide permissive conditions forproliferation.

claims.text: dermoscopy crucial to distinguish SD from psoriasis and tinea capitis
claims.quote: dermoscopy may turn out to be crucial to differentiate between scalp SD and other common scaling disorders, such as psoriasis or tinea capitis

claims.text: maintenance often necessary due to relapsing course
claims.quote: Therefore, due to SD relapsing course, maintenance treatment will often be necessary.

claims.text: diagnosis usually clinical
claims.quote: The diagnosis of SD is usually clinical, and specific laboratory and/or instrumental investigations are seldom required.

claims.quote: When used in shampoo, it may alter hair texture or cause dry or oily hair and scalp.

claims.text: infant SD appears in first three months, lasts until around 12 months
claims.quote: A bimodal distribution occurs in infants, appearing during the first three months of life until around 12 months

claims.text: some authors consider dandruff a non-inflammatory form of SD
claims.quote: Some authors consider dandruff a non-inflammatory form of SD, characterized by fine white scales without underlying erythema

claims.text: bimodal: infancy and adulthood; more common in men; androgens stimulate sebaceous glands
claims.quote: The disease follows a bimodal distribution, with a first peak in infancy and a second in adulthood, particularly among young adults.

claims.text: men more than women; androgens
claims.quote: Seborrheic dermatitis occurs more frequently in men than in women. ... Hormonal imbalances, particularly those involving androgens, stimulate sebaceous gland activity

claims.text: more than 14 species; M. globosa and M. restricta most associated
claims.quote: This genus includes more than 14 species of lipophilic yeasts, with M. globosa and M. restricta being the species most frequently associated with seborrheic dermatitis.

claims.text: lipases and phosphatases; oleic acid penetrates stratum corneum, promotes inflammation, induces desquamation
claims.quote: Among these, oleic acid is particularly relevant, as it penetrates the stratum corneum, promotes inflammation, and induces desquamation

claims.text: TLR2 detection; IL-8, IL-6, TNF-alpha
claims.quote: Keratinocytes detect Malassezia spp. via TLR2, triggering MyD88/NF-κB signaling and promoting the release of IL-8, IL-6, and TNF-α

claims.text: Th1, Th17, Th22 activation
claims.quote: Advances in transcriptomic and microbiome profiling have revealed a complex immunoinflammatory environment in SD, involving predominantly Th1, Th17, and Th22 axes.

claims.text: fungal load vs severity controversial
claims.quote: However, the correlation between fungal load and disease severity remains controversial

claims.text: PDE4 inhibition suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokines
claims.quote: Its inhibition increases intracellular cAMP levels, thereby suppressing proinflammatory cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-17, IL-23, TNF-α)

claims.text: TCIs reduce inflammation without atrophy; non-steroidal alternative for facial SD
claims.quote: TCIs such as pimecrolimus and tacrolimus represent a valuable non-steroidal alternative for the treatment of facial seborrheic dermatitis ... without causing skin atrophy.

claims.text: ceramide moisturizers may help; evidence limited
claims.quote: Although evidence in SD is limited, data from AD support the use of barrier-enhancing emollients containing ceramides, cholesterol, linoleic acid, and niacinamide

claims.text: eyelid involvement: lid hygiene, warm compresses, gentle cleansing, short courses of antibiotics or steroids; interdisciplinary
claims.quote: Management includes lid hygiene with warm compresses and gentle cleansing, artificial tears for dry eye, and short courses of topical antibiotics or corticosteroids for blepharitis when indicated.

claims.text: cold, dry weather exacerbates scaling and itch
claims.quote: cold, dry weather exacerbates scaling and pruritus

claims.text: Parkinson disease associated with SD
claims.quote: Viral infections (HIV, HCV, SARS-CoV-2), neurological disorders such as Parkinson’s disease, and psychological stress have all been associated with increased disease susceptibility.
